summary: LLM inference costs scale linearly with token usage, and well-applied optimization can reduce spend by 50-80% in production systems without degrading output quality. The highest-leverage levers are prompt caching (up to 90% off cached prefix tokens), semantic/response caching (up to ~73% cost reduction in repetitive workloads), and right-sizing models for each task. Most teams see the biggest, fastest wins by fixing retrieval, caching, and model routing before touching prompt wording.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (KV-cache reuse)
techniques.description: Reuses the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated static prompt prefix (system instructions, few-shot examples, long context) so only the dynamic suffix is reprocessed. Cached prefix tokens bill at a steep discount and reduce latency since the model skips recomputation.
techniques.example: Place your large static system prompt and few-shot examples at the start of every request; OpenAI auto-caches prompts over 1024 tokens, while Anthropic uses an explicit cache_control breakpoint to bill the prefix at up to 90% off.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Stores previous responses keyed by the embedding (meaning) of the request rather than an exact string match, returning a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar above a threshold. Eliminates redundant LLM calls entirely for repeated or paraphrased questions.
techniques.savings: Up to 68.8% API call reduction; ~73% cost reduction in high-repetition workloads
techniques.example: Use Redis LangCache or GPTCache to embed incoming queries and serve a stored answer when cosine similarity exceeds 0.95, avoiding a fresh LLM call for 'What's your refund policy?' vs 'How do I get a refund?'

techniques.name: Exact-Match Response Caching
techniques.description: Caches outputs keyed on an exact hash of the full request (prompt + params) so identical calls are served instantly from the cache with zero token cost. Simplest form of caching with no embedding overhead.
techniques.example: Wrap your LLM client with Helicone or LiteLLM caching so deterministic (temperature=0) requests like document classification return cached results on repeat calls.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Right-Sizing
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, reserving frontier models for hard tasks and sending simple ones to budget-tier models. A classifier or heuristic decides the tier per request.
techniques.savings: Up to 16x cost difference between tiers; typically 40-80% overall
techniques.example: Send classification and extraction tasks to GPT-4o-mini ($0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens) and only escalate ambiguous cases to GPT-4o, cutting the same workload from thousands of dollars to under $200.

techniques.name: Retrieval Optimization (RAG tuning)
techniques.description: Fixes the retrieval layer so only the most relevant, de-duplicated chunks are injected into context, rather than stuffing large amounts of loosely relevant text. Reduces input tokens more than any prompt-wording change.
techniques.example: Replace top-k=20 retrieval with a reranker that returns the top 3-5 chunks and strip boilerplate, cutting injected context from 8000 to 2000 tokens per query.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Removes redundant words, whitespace, and low-information tokens from prompts, or uses an LLM-aware compressor to shrink context while preserving meaning. Trims both static and dynamic portions of the prompt.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved context through Microsoft LLMLingua to compress a 3000-token passage to ~1200 tokens before sending it to the model.

techniques.name: Output Token Capping & Structured Output
techniques.description: Limits max_tokens and requests concise or structured (JSON/enum) responses so the model doesn't generate verbose, costly output. Output tokens are often 2-5x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: For a sentiment task, set max_tokens=5 and use structured output to force a single-label response instead of a multi-sentence explanation.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Groups multiple independent inputs into a single call or uses provider batch APIs that process asynchronously at a discount. Reduces per-call overhead and unlocks batch pricing.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% via batch API pricing
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 overnight classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get results within 24 hours at 50% off standard rates.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Streams tokens and stops generation as soon as the needed answer is produced, or uses stop sequences to cut off unneeded continuation. Improves perceived latency and avoids paying for trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Set a stop sequence of '\n\n' when extracting a single value so the model halts after the first line instead of rambling.

techniques.name: Few-Shot Pruning
techniques.description: Reduces the number of in-context examples to the minimum needed for accuracy, or moves examples into a cached prefix. Large example sets inflate every request's input tokens.
techniques.example: Cut a 12-shot prompt to the 3 most representative examples after measuring that accuracy stays within 1% on your eval set.

tools.name: Redis LangCache / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Managed semantic caching layer for LLM apps that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity, reducing redundant calls and cutting cost in repetitive workloads.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud paid tiers usage-based; LangCache managed service priced per usage

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that supports embedding-based similarity matching and pluggable vector stores to serve cached answers for similar queries.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway proxy offering caching, cost tracking, rate limiting, and prompt analytics with a one-line integration.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that routes requests across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, load balancing, fallbacks, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Enterprise plans available; open-source core is free

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with built-in caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), retrieval, and prompt management utilities.

tools.name: LLMLingua (Microsoft)
tools.description: Prompt compression toolkit that uses a small language model to drop low-information tokens, shrinking context while preserving task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic caching, routing, fallbacks, guardrails, and observability across multiple providers.

tools.name: OpenAI / Anthropic Prompt Caching
tools.description: Native provider prompt-caching that discounts repeated prompt prefixes; OpenAI caches automatically for long prompts, Anthropic uses explicit cache_control breakpoints.
tools.pricing_paid: Cache reads billed at 10-50% of normal input price depending on provider

quick_wins: Enable native prompt caching and move all static system instructions and few-shot examples to the start of every request to bill the prefix at up to 90% off.
Add an exact-match and semantic cache (Redis LangCache, GPTCache, or Helicone) in front of your LLM to eliminate redundant calls, cutting repetitive-workload cost by up to ~73%.
Route easy tasks (classification, extraction, summarization) to a budget model like GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash and only escalate hard cases, capturing up to a 16x cost difference.
Cap max_tokens and request concise or structured JSON output so you stop paying for verbose, expensive generated tokens.
Fix retrieval: add a reranker and return the top 3-5 chunks instead of 20, slashing injected context tokens before touching any prompt wording.
